segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Welcome, everybody, to the lovely house and gardens of Rosewood, once the home of the famous writer, Sebastian George.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: He bought the house in 1902 although he had first seen it two years earlier.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: At that time the owners let it out to a tenant because George was too slow making up his mind to buy it.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: When it came back on the_market, there was no hesitation and he bought it immediately, for £9,300, even though the house had no bathroom, no running water upstairs, and no electricity.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: When he came here, he'd been married for ten years.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: During that time, he'd become one of the most famous writers m the English-speaking world.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: His professional success was enormous, but his personal life wasn't as successful.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: He was no longer on speaking terms with his brother and had been devastated by the death at the age-of seven of his elder dau&hter.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Josephine.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Moving to Rosewood allowed the family to start a new life.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: George regarded Rosewood as a pure of a traditional country house of this part of England and did some of his most successful writing here.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: The house and its grounds became the family haven and their escape to privacy and quiet.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: The walls, and the mullioned windows were built of the local sandstone, the tiles on the roofs and the bricks of the chimney stack were baked -from local clay, and the wooden structures inside came from oak trees which grow around here.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Now, please look at the map I've given you of the house and gardens.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: We're here at the Information Centre.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Follow the path marked with the arrow and the first area you come to is the orchard on your left.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: As you go further down the path, there's the kitchen garden on the right and as you go round the first sharp corner you will find. to your left. an area where different types of pear tree have been planted as well as some lovely flowers. and this is known as Pear Alley- designed by George himself.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Next to this is the greenhouse where some exotic plants and fruits are grown.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Follow the path round the second corner and on your right you will see the entrance to the Mulberry Garden with its 500-year-old tree.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Past the Mulberry Garden, follow the path until you reach the front of the house.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: I suggest you spend a good hour wandering around this lovely building.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: A guide takes visitor groups round every two hours.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: If you would like to purchase any of George's books or other souvenirs, then leave the house by the side entrance. where you will find our shop. which is situated between the house and the garage which contains the magnificent old Rolls-Royce car which used to belong to George.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: I expect by this time you may also be in need of a rest and some refreshment.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Most visitors are, so why don't you visit the tea room on the far side of the ~?

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: If you have time, there is a lovely walk down towards the River Dudwell.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: For me, this is the best part of the estate.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: This isn't on the map but it is all clearly signposted.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: You cross the ·ficld which spreads along the banks of the river.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: In spring, this area is well worth a visit.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: QJB Spend a minute or two watching the water pass by underneath as you cross the footbridge, and then continue along the River Walk through the woodland.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: On a hot summer's day the trees along this path provide welcome shade.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Eventually you come to the water mill which used to provide the electricity for the house- only about four hours every evening - in George's time.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: And, finally, for those of you who would like to see stunning views of the surrounding countryside and who are a little bit more energetic, when you return from the mill take the first turning on your left and climb up to the viewpoint.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: You won't regret it.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Enjoy your visit!
